objectives.criterion: Cite the documented behavior for a failing child, a failing scope body and explicit parent cancellation. Distinguish launch exception reporting from await on async.
Use a public thread with a reproducible loop, its dispatcher and a before-and-after cancellation trace. Identify the cooperative checkpoint that changes the outcome.
Provide the exact handler and a test or execution trace proving the allowed exception, the exhausted-retries case and propagation of cancellation.
Identify a licensed, revision-pinned project, its CoroutineScope creation and its close or stop call site. Explain which work the owner cancels.
Compare delivery, replay, suspension and overflow using exact buffer settings for both APIs. Attach documentation or a runnable observation for the zero-subscriber case.
Find a documented adapter or tested pattern showing cancellation ownership, a blocked read and one observed cleanup. State the assumptions about interruptible I/O.
Find a benchmark or profile with stated parallelism, task duration, JVM and library versions. Extract throughput, tail latency and thread counts with the units shown.
Tie the migration to a versioned guide and a test that shares a TestCoroutineScheduler. Record which dispatchers advance virtual time and which delays remain real.
Provide publication metadata and a page or section describing parent-child task lifetimes. Specify whether its claims are a model, an implementation result or an empirical finding.
Quote a short verbatim passage with the API symbol, version and section. Separate the standard select rule from any statement about an unbiased variant.
Cite a versioned default hierarchy description, show the applicable target groups and indicate which source sets depend on commonMain for one concrete target matrix.
Preserve the minimal target matrix, dependency placement, diagnostic and version from the thread. Cite the observed resolution and any unresolved platform limitation.
Retrieve declared signatures, actual source-set paths and a named common test. Identify what the test proves without assuming wall-clock determinism on each host.
Provide license, revision, shared model file and both entrypoint paths. Give one concrete dependency path from a platform entrypoint to shared logic.
Give the build and consumption entrypoints, host prerequisites, dependency handling and distribution artifacts for the same stated integration scenario.
Find a build layout with an explicit platform dependency boundary and a reproducible compile check for at least one JVM and one Native target.
Record task names, clean versus incremental action, machine and plugin version. Extract timings for each phase or document which phase was not identified.
Use versioned compatibility or release notes, name at least one relevant interop feature, and identify browser or tooling prerequisites and known unsupported cases.
Identify the publication and corpus, how it defines shared code, and an extractable measurement. Record limits such as sample size, UI sharing or build tooling.
Quote the precise eligibility rule with its version and anchor. Retain a minimal cited example or a documented condition that prevents careless generalization.
Cite the API guide's registration and lifecycle hooks. Include a route-scoped example and tie a documented interception phase to the rejected-call behavior.
Require the framework/engine version, an observable thread or latency symptom, and the author's repro or resulting fix. Label unverified suggestions separately.
Provide the response-writing and cleanup paths with a test or verified lifecycle reference. Note how the example controls buffering or backpressure.
Identify a revision and license, the filter code, its composition point and a test or example proving that the identifier reaches the downstream handler.
Compare one equivalent suspending endpoint in both frameworks. Show context propagation and disconnect/cancellation evidence for named dependency versions.
Find an implementation or documentation pattern with explicit context scope and a test that proves identifier continuity and credential exclusion.
Extract hardware, warm-up, engine versions, request mix, throughput and p95 or p99 latency. Record whether socket reuse and resource limits are held fixed.
Return versioned support references or BOM evidence, with a minimal compatibility example and a known mismatch or a precise statement of the matrix boundary.
Provide author, title, venue and date, then extract workload, comparator and at least one measured outcome. Note unsupported or subjective conclusions.
Quote the relevant passage and identify its context, framework version and annotation or configuration referenced. Separate the general guidance from example details.
Locate the versioned JVM documentation for both options. Give the meaning of each bound, applicability and a documented condition for exceeding the soft target.
Preserve JVM version, container limit and the observed heap/native/RSS evidence. Identify whether the diagnosis used Native Memory Tracking, OS accounting or another concrete measurement.
Provide the selected JFR event names, the recording options and a concrete output field that identifies allocation cost. State whether sampled events report estimates or exact counts.
Provide license, version or revision, an entrypoint for a heap dump and one verifiable example that distinguishes shallow size from retained size.
Compare stated allocation and reclamation behavior for matching JDK releases. Cite the applicable object-size terminology and identify which observations need measurement.
Find a procedure that identifies the ownership path from a GC root, demonstrates positive and negative controls, and separates temporary liveness from durable retention.
Extract heap settings, collector, cache workload, live-set or allocation data, and pause or latency percentiles. Record the evidence connecting the cache to a GC cost.
Identify releases where the relevant flags change behavior, the supported migration options and a sourced flag-by-flag compatibility example.
Give publication metadata and one observed object-age distribution or collection result. State the workloads and distinguish measured findings from theoretical arguments.
Quote the entry with version and section. Preserve the memory domain it names and any default or scope qualification relevant to a direct-buffer limit.
Cite the factory and inherited close contract. Explain task completion and interruption semantics using exact referenced statements.
Require the cited JDK release, the operation under observation and a recorded trace or event. Distinguish a measured pin from speculation based on synchronization alone.
Provide the task submission, timeout and cancellation/cleanup code plus a test or trace that shows at least one task exceeds the deadline.
Provide license, version, the request-executor implementation and its configuration or minimal test path. Distinguish actual request handling from a marketing claim.
Give comparable bounds on active calls and outstanding tasks, and cite concrete evidence about queuing, admission and cancellation behavior.
Find a documented pattern with lexical ownership or explicit cleanup and a reproducible check of object lifetime after a request ends.
Record version, machine, concurrency, queueing policy, throughput and tail latency. Identify which cost is CPU work and which is waiting.
Use the relevant JEP or release notes. Tie each covered and uncovered case to the release and verify a documented example or event.
Provide bibliographic data, the comparator, workloads and a quantitative result. Include the author's stated limitations or explain why the experiment cannot establish a universal speedup.
Quote the relevant short statement and its context. Preserve the distinction between reuse of virtual threads and limiting access to a scarce service.
Cite versioned membership guidance. Capture catch-up requirements, failure conditions and the membership impact expressed by the documentation.
Extract the configured consistency mode, timeline and a minimal repro or diagnosis from participants. Separate an application expectation mismatch from a replication defect.
Cite the token allocation and writer comparison. Identify a reproducible local test in which a stale write is rejected after a new owner is admitted.
Provide project license and revision, a source path for snapshot installation and a test proving the follower catches up after old log entries become unavailable.
Compare causal information, metadata growth and wall-clock properties. Use a concrete event pair as evidence of what each model can and cannot distinguish.
Find a tested protocol showing where database transactions end and what durable cursor or key stores the delivery state. Include an observed crash-and-replay case.
Extract region layout, quorum/ack policy, workload and latency percentiles. Compare against a documented baseline with the same payload and durability contract.
Cite the versioned client/broker guidance and one staged upgrade sequence. Identify what a mixed-version or mixed-strategy test demonstrates.
Give metadata and the theorem's location, state the specified consistency/availability model and include the treatment of partitions. Avoid extrapolating beyond its assumptions.
Quote a short precise passage with section/page and the qualification about current-term entries. Retain the explanation or figure reference needed to interpret it.
Cite versioned message-processing documentation explaining anchoring, ack/fail and timeout. Provide an exact configuration key or API identifier for each relevant boundary.
Extract the topology and Storm version, observed signals and the specific change tested. Label a proposed tuning suggestion separately from confirmed outcome.
Provide the emit, ack and fail call sites plus a test or documented trace that shows the success path and one failure path.
Provide license and revision, topology builder call sites, the grouped fields and a README or test observation that establishes why those fields matter.
Compare what identifiers each retains, when effects become visible and what guarantee depends on the source/state adapter. Use versioned references for the same failure scenario.
Find implementation or operator evidence of a drain or bounded shutdown protocol. Verify which state or metric confirms completion before the worker exits and how remaining work is classified.
Record versions, topology grouping, worker/executor counts, offered load, throughput and at least one queue or tail-latency observation. Identify the first evidenced bottleneck.
Name the release pair and cite concrete old and new configuration or metrics identifiers. Include a migration check for the behavior, not only a renamed key.
Provide author, title and venue, describe the workload and acknowledgement configuration, and extract measured overhead or throughput with the reported limitations.
Quote the applicable short statement with release and symbol. Distinguish the maximum pending tuple count from queue size or message timeout.
Identify the documented accounting rules, the relevant configuration knobs, and the conditions under which reservations can trigger a flush.
Find a public thread with two distinguishable symptoms and preserve the cited stall counters or level statistics, the WAL observations, and the release context.
Provide a concrete API example with the write options, status handling, and source locations that document atomicity and sync behavior.
Link an upstream source revision to the public checkpoint API and the implementation that manages the resource lifetime.
Compare consistency boundaries, what is copied, and how restoration works using documentation or source for both paths.
Describe a verified operational sequence with an explicit consistent snapshot, reader and writer boundaries, integrity checks, and rollback points.
Preserve the dataset, cache and table settings, read workload, and measured latency or memory data from each reported comparison.
Name the producer and reader versions, cite the configuration or format contract, and distinguish supported file opening from unsupported downgrade assumptions.
Identify a named paper or technical report, state its model assumptions, and tie a documented compaction option to the relevant mechanism.
Quote a short passage with the exact source symbol, file or documentation section, and source revision or release.
Cite the documented selection rule and a reproducible inspection command with the relevant server version.
Preserve the reported transaction age or vacuum counters, distinguish diagnosis from advice, and cite the thread and relevant documentation.
Include the table setup, both commands, the expected effect on new and existing rows, and authoritative documentation for the tested release.
Identify the source revision, the public pool mode contract, and a test or implementation location that supports the limitation.
Compare both plans against documented data correlation assumptions, index size, and block rechecks under a stated workload.
Give a staged SQL plan with transaction boundaries, lock modes, verification queries, and a rollback boundary for partial backfills.
Find a reproducible measurement that reports the number of sessions, plan shape, memory setting, spill diagnostics, and runtime for each run.
Cite documentation for the version pair and identify the extension library dependencies and compatibility checks relevant to the upgrade.
Identify the paper or technical report, the predicate and dataset setup, and actual versus estimated cardinalities or query costs.
Return a short exact quotation with its manual section and PostgreSQL version, and keep any interpretation separate.
Cite the isolation definition and two named engine manuals, separating minimum guarantees from each engine's stronger behavior.
Select a public explanation that presents the competing transaction order and show why its observations fit one anomaly instead of the other.
Provide a complete small schema, ordered read and write steps, expected rows for both cases, and the engine and isolation settings.
Tie the stated snapshot boundary to a concrete SQLite test or source revision and record what the reader observes before and after restarting its transaction.
Contrast whether either transaction waits or aborts in a named implementation of each approach, and record the assumptions behind the comparison.
Describe which code must run again, where an idempotency key or outbox is stored, and how failure before or after commit is distinguished.
Find a controlled or published benchmark with duration and contention settings, successful commit throughput, and a separately reported abort count.
Cite versioned source material for both engines that covers default isolation, locking versus ordinary reads, and a migration case affected by the difference.
Identify the publication and the formal definitions used for graph edges and cycles, and include a correctly sourced example history.
Return a short quote with the publication, page or section, and enough surrounding terminology to distinguish commit conflicts from ordinary reads.
Cite a language or compiler source for the rule and include a small accepted example paired with a variant that remains rejected.
Find a thread with the original diagnostic, the guard lifetime explanation, and at least one documented ownership-preserving alternative.
Provide a minimal compiling example with the safe API, its index condition, and checks showing that writes reach the expected disjoint ranges.
Cite upstream allocation and drop code or documentation for both plain arena allocations and an owning wrapper, using a specific revision or release.
Compare ownership lifetime, clone and allocation costs, and the implications for retaining a small token from a large input.
Give an offset-based or borrowed-input interface with a concrete example and show how each alternative prevents dangling storage references.
Use or describe a reproducible comparison with varied escape frequency and report allocated bytes and execution time alongside the corpus shape.
Record the relevant language release and edition using official release or edition notes, with a minimal example for the compatibility boundary.
Identify the paper, one abstraction it models, the invariant that justifies its public API, and the scope of the formal guarantee.
Return a short exact quotation with the book chapter or revision and distinguish that wording from an explanation of non-lexical lifetimes.
Cite the exact trait documentation and identify the requirements on wake registration and returning without blocking the executor.
Preserve the public example or log, identify what caused the blocked progress, and link the proposed correction to the documented guard semantics.
Provide a runnable short example and verify capacity, channel closure, and the delivery of already accepted messages without unbounded buffering.
Use a tagged release or source revision to trace runnable queue insertion, waiter notification, and the functions responsible for polling.
Give a versioned behavior table supported by documentation or tests, including which work is cancelled and which work is only no longer polled.
Show where partial state remains owned across cancellation and verify the behavior on an interruption between header and payload bytes.
Provide a reproducible measurement plan or published workload with thread counts, timing breakdown, queue depth, and a blocking-work control.
Cite the toolchain and crate versions plus minimal trait examples that demonstrate the different bounds or dispatch behavior.
Identify the published study and scheduler configurations and preserve the actual throughput and tail-latency measurements with workload context.
Quote the relevant small documentation passage and cite its crate version and method section.
Cite the API contract for the constructor and the constraints that prevent overlap or out-of-bounds indexing.
Find a public minimal input and observed output and cite the array layout or BLAS interface contract used to explain the mismatch.
Provide a runnable example with an explicit population or sample definition and verify it against a known data sequence and boundary cases.
Cite the public API and build features at a release or revision and verify at least one representative decomposition entry point.
Compare rounding, exactness at the chosen scale, overflow, and a worked boundary case using explicit numeric assumptions.
Describe fixed partition and merge ordering, document the floating-point accuracy limitations, and give a small verification strategy using the same input and thread count changes.
Preserve transform sizes, plan initialization cost, warmed throughput, allocation behavior, and the crate version from a reproducible benchmark or published measurements.
Name the conversion API or interoperability crate and versions, and distinguish borrowed views, owned conversions, and copies with evidence.
Identify the source and relevant theorem or experiment and state the rounding and input-order assumptions before comparing the methods.
Return the minimal relevant quotation with the API path and Rust version, and keep any hardware-specific commentary separate.
Locate the versioned scoring documentation or source and relate both parameters to the term-frequency and field-length components.
Use a public diagnostic example or token trace, preserve the analyzer settings, and cite the source that explains the position behavior.
Provide runnable or fully inspectable code with input lists and a checked output order, including the rule for duplicate IDs.
Cite the index configuration plus query and indexing code or tests at a public source revision.
Find a labeled workload or reported evaluation that keeps corpus and query set constant and reports the error cases and retrieval metrics for both approaches.
Give a documented grouping or version-aware judgment method and explain which precision or recall denominator it uses without counting duplicate copies as corroboration.
Use a reproducible profile or published measurements with query mix, merge timing, thread settings, and separate p95 or p99 observations.
Identify a specific engine's versioned analyzer and index contract, show how persisted tokens are affected, and cite a migration or reindex boundary.
Cite the publication and equation or metric definition, and walk through a sourced example without assuming an unjudged document is truly irrelevant.
Quote the relevant short passage with its track, year, or tool version and identify the metric to avoid generalizing to every TREC measure.
Use the official manual for one named release. Cite the dictionary result types and a traceable configuration example distinguishing stop words from unrecognized tokens.
Find a public issue or discussion with a reproducible shard comparison, the reported scoring configuration, and a reply distinguishing measured observations from proposed explanations.
Cite a runnable schema and code excerpt with a stable source revision. Include sample input, an expected matching row, and a nonmatching row for the same phrase.
Trace the IndexWriter and reader refresh paths in one release. Distinguish segment visibility from the state that survives a process restart.
Support a side-by-side table with documented token and relevance behavior plus a controlled example showing substring-only, token-only, and equal-match cases.
Find a documented shadow-index or reindex example with explicit locale settings, versioned validation queries, a switchover criterion, and a rollback condition.
Accept measurements only with corpus size, vocabulary or prefix selectivity, fixed top-K, benchmark revision, and a stated cache condition.
Cite the release-specific support policy and a test or tool example with the exact index writer and reader versions. Separate read compatibility from write compatibility.
Identify primary publications and page or equation references for both scoring models. Explain term weighting using their definitions and leave dataset-dependent performance unclaimed.
Return the exact short passage with section and release, plus its documented example. Distinguish lexeme positions from character distance.
Cite the official API for one release and use three small hand-checkable vectors. Verify the documented treatment of empty vectors and avoid inferring behavior for a different release.
Return the example pair, the reported representation or threshold, and evidence separating the observed false positive from proposed boilerplate-removal remedies.
Keep an attributed code excerpt and paired tests for Unicode-equivalent spellings and reordered words. Cite the normalization form, shingle width, and repository revision.
Find one maintained or released implementation and trace its candidate-index API to code and tests. Describe which result scores are computed by indexing and which by comparison.
Compare documented representation, score meaning, and one controlled hand-checkable perturbation for each method. Identify parameters that make observed scores incomparable.
Find or derive from a documented implementation a clear normalization and verification split. Supply an auditable set with a true boilerplate duplicate and a version-specific counterexample.
Require one dataset, fixed embeddings and top-K, a reference exact search, reported hardware, and at least two parameter settings. Attribute each measured quantity to its source.
Require compatibility guidance for dimensions and seed, discovery of the serialization format, and a versioned positive round trip or a documented incompatibility.
Cite a primary paper with publication metadata and exact definitions. Point to the equation or theorem for sketch comparison and distinguish it from approximate implementation behavior.
Return the exact short assertion with release and section, a citation to the formula on that page, and an indication of the input assumption.
Cite versioned WARC documentation with linked example records. Trace the related identifier and show why target URI alone cannot establish that the records are from the same capture.
Find a public thread with original capture evidence, replay evidence, and a reply that identifies the missing subresource. Preserve any stated distinction from a capture or decoding failure.
Provide cited code and a reproducible small fixture with the digest expected from the stored response. Show truncation or modified bytes being reported as a failed verification.
Find the relevant code in a tagged release and trace persisted run state to documented resume behavior. Identify a test or example that checks identity continuity across the restart.
Compare published format requirements for records, indexes, manifests, and provenance. Include one case where the captured document is present but standalone replay metadata is missing.
Find a documented content-addressed archive design or recovery protocol. Specify the observable outcomes for crashes before publication and after body publication but before index commit.
Require the archive format, compression settings, corpus, and a warmed-versus-cold or explicitly uncached read protocol. Report throughput and latency separately.
Name the parser and release, cite the versioned WARC specification, and locate a fixture or compatibility note showing accepted fields or an explicit unsupported case.
Cite the original published specification or paper and the exact datetime-negotiation sequence. Distinguish original resource identity from its archived representation.
Return a short exact quote with standard version and section. Cross-reference a complete example showing the revisit record and the record it refers to.
Cite versioned controller documentation and source or an example that connects cache readiness to the beginning of reconciliation.
Identify a public development thread and extract separately attributed positions. Include the feature version discussed and an example whose outcome can be verified from declared behavior.
Cite one project-owned task implementation and its test. Trace the annotated inputs and outputs, how a cache hit is observed, and a change that invalidates the hit.
Use a tagged Kafka source tree and architecture document. Identify the relevant roles and trace a metadata update from an owning component to a broker consumer.
Compare one named storage mode for each system, such as WAL-enabled SQLite and PostgreSQL default concurrency. Cite the actual lock or transaction boundaries and a failure/readback example.
Find published code or documentation with an explicit acceptance record, ownership claim, replay/idempotency rule, and a restart test. Distinguish queue liveness from completed work.
Use an explained collector configuration and a published or reproducible controlled measurement. Cite queue size, the chosen load, and how dropped data and successful delivery were observed.
Cite the versioned interoperability spec and a cross-library fixture with exact library versions. Identify field ownership and release-callback assumptions beyond simple schema equality.
Identify the primary publication. Attribute the comparison to the relevant section and use its own worked example rather than inferred architectural slogans.
Return a short exact statement with release or stable revision and the documented example. Distinguish visibility of the re-export from the private module that defines the type.
Cite official Javadoc with the exact JUnit version. Include one controlled example that reveals the thread relationship and observes timeout behavior.
Find a public thread with a reproducible setup, an observed failing condition, and evidence identifying shared state or another cause. Note whether the reported patch was verified.
Find code that uses explicit synchronization and finite waits. Cite the assertion on child state and the cleanup checks for timeout or failure.
Cite a release and trace one example test through its operation generator and verifier. Use source or documentation to distinguish stress mode from model checking.
Compare one documented workload reproduced under both strategies. Cite what is observable with fixed schedules, what can be missed, and why passing differs from exhaustive correctness.
Find a test or implementation that injects failure after commit but before response. Trace the replay identity and provide evidence for both the resulting count and retained record content.
Require a fixed runner, suite, Java version, measurements for more than one fork setting, and both wall time and memory. Identify parallelism limits and isolation settings.
Cite the release-specific signal and subprocess contracts. Distinguish invoking an in-process handler, delivering a console event, and terminating without a cooperative signal.
Find a primary publication with publication metadata and an example. Cite the operation-independence assumption and distinguish its coverage from enumerating all scheduler choices.
Return the short exact Java API passage and release, identify the predecessor and successor actions, and preserve the distinction between return modes.
Provide edition, publication year, rights statement covering the selected copy, and a page-level pointer to the explanation. Distinguish the original text from editorial annotation.
Find a publicly readable discussion naming the edition and disputed symbol or passage; verify the discrepancy against a scanned page when rights and access are explicit.

Use a public-domain primary work with page evidence, supply a short attributed or example implementation, and show predicted outputs on a small input. Distinguish reconstruction from historical source code.
Select a technical title with the connection evidenced, capture catalog identity, edition and publication year, available file types, plus the applicable rights notice.
Cite exact editions and corresponding propositions, compare one named diagram marking and notation, and distinguish substantive geometric changes from editorial renaming.

Find a public-domain table and compare an exact row against its scan. Identify a suspect character, preserve its place in the table, and cite a transcription or encoding practice for marking uncertainty.
Separate reported operation counts, reported physical timing, and modern reproduction. Return page-level evidence and leave conversions or speed comparisons unclaimed when the inputs are missing.
Use a named edition and one sourced worked example. Record the original units and symbols, cite a documented conversion or correspondence, and identify any ambiguous notation without guessing.
Cite a public-domain original edition with the page and a separate published historical discussion. Keep the original symbol, named operation, and scope distinct from later terminology.
Return a short quote with author, edition, page or section, and a rights-identified scan. Verify that quotation and transcription reflect the same edition.
